The correlation between the tests of a spicy() result

Source: R/testCorrelation.R
testCorrelation.Rd

The tests of pairs that share a cell type, or that are nested (a cell type and a group containing it), are correlated through the patients they share. testCorrelation() estimates the correlation between every two pairs' tests from the one fit, for a correction for multiple testing that uses it in place of independence.

Usage

testCorrelation(
  x,
  method = c("cr2", "permutation"),
  nPermutations = 1000,
  cores = 1
)

Arguments

x

The output of spicy() (or kontextualEngine()) with two conditions, one radius (or k), no adjustment (no covariates, adjustAbundance = FALSE) and variance = "cr2".

method

"cr2" (the default) or "permutation".

nPermutations

The number of permutations for method = "permutation".

cores

The number of threads for method = "permutation".

Value

A symmetric matrix with one row and one column per row of x$cellResults (the same row names): the estimated correlation between the pairs' tests. The diagonal is 1, and rows and columns of pairs not tested (or, by permutation, whose z is the same in every permutation) are NA.

Details

Each pair's difference between conditions is a weighted mean over patients: a patient's summary is the weighted mean of its images' effects (x$pairwiseAssoc) with the images' weights (x$imageWeights), and its weight is the sum of its images' weights times its condition's information (x$conditionInformation).

method = "cr2": each patient's CR2 influence on the difference, psi = h (summary - its condition's mean) / sqrt(1 - h) with h the patient's share of its condition's weight, negated in the reference condition. Its squares sum to the test's squared standard error, and the cross-products of two pairs' influences, divided by the two standard errors, estimate the correlation of their differences. It is noisy when a few patients carry most of a pair's weight and one condition is small.

method = "permutation": the conditions are permuted over the patients nPermutations times; for each permutation every test is recomputed in closed form from the patients' summaries and weights (each condition's weighted mean, its CR2 variance and Satterthwaite df, as spicy() computes them; the between-patient variance is held at the fit's, and of spicy()'s rules for not testing a pair only the need for two patients in each condition is applied), and its p-value is turned into a z with the sign of its (skewness-corrected) t (0 when a condition has fewer than two of the pair's patients). The correlation of the tests' z over the permutations is returned. The permutations come from a fixed seed, so a result always gives the same matrix, in R and in Python.

See also

spicy()

Examples

data("diabetesData")
cells <- diabetesData[, diabetesData$stage != "Long-duration"]
res <- spicy(cells, condition = "stage", subject = "case", r = 50, from = c("Tc", "Th"), to = c("beta", "alpha"))
testCorrelation(res)
#>            Tc__beta Tc__alpha  Th__beta Th__alpha
#> Tc__beta  1.0000000 0.9336402 0.7045028 0.7501011
#> Tc__alpha 0.9336402 1.0000000 0.8968579 0.8537341
#> Th__beta  0.7045028 0.8968579 1.0000000 0.8805660
#> Th__alpha 0.7501011 0.8537341 0.8805660 1.0000000
testCorrelation(res, method = "permutation", nPermutations = 200)
#>            Tc__beta Tc__alpha  Th__beta Th__alpha
#> Tc__beta  1.0000000 0.9237687 0.7286594 0.7908283
#> Tc__alpha 0.9237687 1.0000000 0.8738504 0.8915030
#> Th__beta  0.7286594 0.8738504 1.0000000 0.8671063
#> Th__alpha 0.7908283 0.8915030 0.8671063 1.0000000
